newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen down on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen down on Wednesday.

text.p: Polish shares on Tuesday rose for the fourth session running but analysts said a fall was likely on Wednesday, signalled by strong selling after fixing and a fall by the WIG 20 index in continuous trade.
Analysts said that though some prices were attractive at current levels the market may be fearing possible falls on Western bourses, which left most demand speculative and local.

"Investors are currently inclined to make quick profits so they're investing in small firms which either grow by 10 percent or not at all," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.
Analysts said the forthcoming April public offerings of paper firm Celuloza Swiecie SA and metals trader Impexmetal SA could be keeping capital from listed stocks.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.6 percent to 16,244.7 points and turnover rose 4.1 percent to 182.3 million zlotys ($58.9 million) on all three markets. Gainers led losers by 53 to 26 with 13 stocks flat.
Analysts were surprised by the scale of tyre maker Debica's rise, which surged 9.9 percent in light trade.
They said furniture maker Swarzedz could extend its 9.5-percent gain on Tuesday, the day after the firm signed a debt restructuring deal with creditors.

Analysts said cable maker Kable, whose trade was suspended on Tuesday, should rise on Wednesday after Danish 50-percent owner NKT Cables announced a public tender offer to buy Kable's remaining one million shares at 41 zlotys each ($13.2).

Analysts said Tuesday's news that food prices rose 0.2 percent in March's final third and 0.5 percent since late February was expected by the market, which was more preoccupied with information concerning interest rates abroad.
